clue.text: The way of the Censor with conspirators

definitions.text: The way of the Censor with conspirators

parts.words: The way of the Censor with conspirators
parts.note: Cato the Elder was Rome's famous Censor, and a London street named after him gave its name to the 1820 plot to murder the Cabinet

explanation.surface: A question of how a strict Roman magistrate dealt with plotters.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cato Street Conspiracy of 1820 was a plot to murder the British Cabinet, hatched in a loft in a London street; the street is read as the 'way' belonging to Cato the Censor.
explanation.definitionFit: The London street where the 1820 plotters gathered shares its name with Cato, the Roman Censor.

clue.text: All circle round the river god

indicators.note: round means the first word goes around another piece

parts.note: taken as written, in capitals
the Po is Italy's longest river
a circle is the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Everyone circles a river god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'river god' reads as one phrase, but the river is wordplay and the definition is just 'god'.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollo was the Greek and Roman deity of the sun, music and prophecy.

clue.text: Reason for celebration ?

definitions.meaning: a cause or ground, as in having no call to complain

explanation.definitionFit: It means a cause or ground for something, and also a special event or festivity.

clue.text: River duel involved a large number — and Carroll's battler

parts.note: the Tweed is the river on the English-Scottish border

indicators.note: involved means twisted up, so the letters of duel are rearranged

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A big river fight joined by many, involving Lewis Carroll's fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' turns DUEL into LEDU; M is a thousand. Tweedledum and Tweedledee agree to have a battle in Through the Looking-Glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweedledum agrees to a fight with his twin over a rattle in Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass.

clue.text: Girl appears the day before the row

parts.note: the eve of an event is the day before it
a line is a row

explanation.surface: A girl turns up the day before a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel but means a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Eveline is a girl's given name, the title of a Joyce story.

clue.text: Article found under cask of fish

indicators.note: in a down clue, under puts this piece below the cask

parts.note: a tun is a large cask
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An item in a barrel of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'found under' places A below TUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large sea fish, often canned.

clue.text: Othello character appears in outfit used in cowboy show.

indicators.note: used in means this piece goes inside the show's letters

parts.note: a rodeo is a show of cowboy skills
a rig is an outfit of clothes

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare character appears in costume at a Wild West show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outfit' looks like costume for the show, but it means a set of clothes, slipped inside the show's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Roderigo is the foolish Venetian gulled by Iago in Shakespeare's Othello.

clue.text: Vegetarian jollifications leaving us full of high spirits?

definitions.text: Vegetarian jollifications leaving us full of high spirits?

parts.words: Vegetarian jollifications leaving us full of high spirits?
parts.note: a works outing or jolly party, taken literally as a meal of pulses that leaves diners full of wind

explanation.walkthrough: The British term for a works dinner or jolly outing, also called a beano, is read literally as a feast of beans, with 'high spirits' hinting at wind.
explanation.definitionFit: These are lively parties or outings with food, and also literally meals of pulses.

clue.text: Ruined-but not cheated?

definitions.meaning: ruined, as in a person brought to ruin

explanation.definitionFit: Ruined is a standard synonym; split into un- plus 'done', slang for swindled, it means not swindled.

clue.text: What builders use for start of construction on island

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, here taken from construction

parts.note: taken as written
Crete is the large Greek island

explanation.surface: A remark about what goes into beginning a building project on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' takes only the opening letter C of 'construction'; ON is the clue's own word, and CRETE the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Builders pour this mix of cement, sand and gravel for foundations and walls.

clue.text: Get to know about article made of tough stuff

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to learn something is to get to know it
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Advice to study a piece about hard-wearing material.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an article in a magazine; here it is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: Leathern is an old adjective for things made of hide, a tough material.

clue.text: First item sold by French author

parts.note: an item sold at auction is a lot
I is the Roman numeral one, so first

explanation.surface: The opening lot at an auction goes to a French writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Pierre Loti was a French novelist of the late nineteenth century; 'First' gives I, the Roman one, placed after LOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre Loti, author of Pêcheur d'Islande, was a celebrated French novelist and naval officer.

clue.text: Harbour dues become less onerous with time

parts.note: to grow lighter is to become less burdensome, read as the adjective lighter
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Port charges get lighter over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'dues become' as subject and verb, but the definition stops at 'dues'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighterage is the fee paid for carrying goods by barge between ship and quay in port.

clue.text: Handy wrinkle for rescue work?

parts.note: a crease on the palm read by palmists, whose name turned round suggests the rope thrown to save someone

explanation.walkthrough: Palmists read a crease on the hand by this name; 'Handy' means on the hand, and the lifeline thrown in a rescue is the same words reversed in order. The grid's LINE OF FIRE was a guess; both differing squares are unchecked.
explanation.definitionFit: The palmist's crease on the hand predicting longevity bears this name, echoing the rope thrown to save someone.

clue.text: Public needs a monarch that's going to the front

parts.note: overt means open, public
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: The people need a king who goes to the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front' suggests war, but the definition means passing others.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing another vehicle means moving into the lead, getting ahead.

clue.text: Poor range of foreign war weapon

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters of range are in bad shape and rearranged

parts.note: de is French for of

explanation.surface: A complaint that a foreign war weapon has poor range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges RANGE to GRENA; 'of foreign' is DE, French for 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small bomb thrown by hand in battle.

clue.text: Physicist calls for a German beer?

parts.note: ein is German for a
a stein is a beer mug, standing for beer

explanation.surface: A scientist orders a German beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calls for' joins the definition to the order 'ein Stein', German for a beer mug.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein was the physicist behind the theory of relativity.

clue.text: Quarters for old salts ?

definitions.meaning: the four quarters of the year: spring, summer, autumn and winter
old salts are sailors, read as sons of the sea

explanation.definitionFit: Each is a quarter of the year; split as sea sons they are sailors, sons of the ocean.

clue.text: One after another appearing in the Mitre as I arranged

indicators.note: arranged means these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Something lines up in order at the Mitre, a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' reorders the letters of MITRE AS I.
explanation.definitionFit: Seriatim is Latin for in series, point by point in order.

clue.text: One of a dozen trying to do his duty ?

definitions.text: One of a dozen trying to do his duty

parts.words: One of a dozen trying to do his duty
parts.note: trying means hearing a court case, and a dozen citizens sit in judgement on the verdict

explanation.walkthrough: 'trying' means judging a case at court, not attempting, and juries have twelve members.
explanation.definitionFit: A juror is one of twelve citizens hearing a trial.

clue.text: Equivalent of so much in French money

parts.note: tant is French for so much
an amount is a sum of money

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a sum in French money comes to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' signals the French word TANT; AMOUNT is the sum of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantamount to something means equal to it in effect, so equivalent.

clue.text: Measures, connected with catches in Test, perhaps ?

parts.words: connected with catches in Test, perhaps
parts.note: angling poles used to land fish in the River Test, a famous Hampshire trout river, not cricket catches in a Test match

explanation.walkthrough: A rod is an old unit of length. The Test here is a Hampshire trout river, not a cricket Test match, so the catches are fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod or perch is an old unit of length of five and a half yards, so rods are measures; fishing rods catch trout.

clue.text: N.U.R. aid in distributing Eastern fruit

indicators.note: distributing means spreading the letters out into a new order

parts.note: NUR is the National Union of Railwaymen, a former British trade union

explanation.surface: A rail union's aid in delivering fruit from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in distributing' shuffles NUR and AID together.
explanation.definitionFit: The durian is a large spiky Southeast Asian fruit famous for its smell.

clue.text: Fish, including those processed in Bute

indicators.note: including means the fish holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a ray is a flat fish

indicators.note: processed means the letters of those are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A fish dish with processed ingredients from a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: Rothesay is the main town on the Scottish island of Bute, so 'in Bute' defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rothesay is the chief town on the island of Bute, in the Firth of Clyde.

clue.text: These empires appear to be included

indicators.note: to be included says the letters sit inside the words of These empires

explanation.surface: These empires seem to be included.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'theSE EMpires'.
explanation.definitionFit: To seem is to give an appearance of being.

clue.text: Uphold chief anti-reformer

parts.note: main means chief, principal

indicators.note: a reformer reshapes things, so the letters of anti are reformed

explanation.surface: A head opponent of reform holds firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anti-reformer' reads as one hyphenated word, but it splits into the fodder and its anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To uphold a claim or a building is to keep it up, preserve it.

clue.text: Brook divides notes in bars

indicators.note: divides means one piece goes between the others and splits them

parts.note: G and E are notes of the musical scale
a rill is a small brook

explanation.surface: A stream splits musical notes in the bars of a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divides' puts RILL between the notes G and E. 'bars' suggests music but is a grating.
explanation.definitionFit: A grille is a grating of metal bars over a window or opening.

clue.text: Bosses write island representative about me

parts.note: the Isle of Man

indicators.note: about means the representative's letters go round the other word

parts.note: an agent acts as a representative
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to write to the island's representative about oneself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'write' is only a joining word here; MAN is the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The people running a firm, the bosses collectively, are its directors and executives.
